clips.title: AWS re:Invent 2022 - Minimizing the production impact of ML model updates w/shadow testing (AIM343)
clips.why: Shadow testing comes from machine learning teams: the new model gets real traffic, but its answers never reach a user. It is exactly our shadow stage, explained by the people who use it daily.
look: The new version sees the same real requests as the live one, so the comparison is fair.
Its answers are recorded and compared, but never shown to the user. That is our shadow fix, saved to S3 and never opened as a PR.
Promotion happens only after someone looks at the comparison.
clips.after: Our weekly shadow report is the comparison step: each shadow fix next to the fix a person really made for the same failure.

clips.title: Andrej Karpathy: Software Is Changing (Again)
clips.why: Karpathy argues for keeping AI on a short leash: small changes that a person can check quickly, in a fast loop between generating and verifying.
look: Why a huge change from an AI is a problem even when it is right: the person checking it becomes the slow part.
Small, checkable pieces keep the human part of the loop fast.
clips.after: Our noise rules are that leash for routines: one open PR at a time, always a draft first, and small changes a reviewer can check in minutes.

clips.title: Andrej Karpathy: Software Is Changing (Again)
clips.why: His Tesla Autopilot story shows how long it takes to hand over autonomy safely, and his autonomy slider is the same idea as our three stages.
look: The autonomy slider: the same tool can act with little or a lot of independence, and you choose where to set it.
Autonomy grows slowly, after a lot of evidence, not after one impressive demo.
clips.after: Shadow, drafts and normal are three positions on that slider, and only evidence plus a person's reviewed yes moves a routine to the right.

practice.q: fe-ci-fixer is in shadow. Main goes red, the fixer finds a correct one-line fix and proves it. What happens to the fix?

options.text: It opens a draft PR and pings only the owner
options.why: That is the drafts stage. In shadow nothing is opened.

options.text: It is saved to S3 with its proof for the weekly shadow report, and nobody is pinged
options.why: Shadow does all the work and skips only the part that costs people's attention.

options.text: It is thrown away, because shadow runs are only for testing the trigger
options.why: The saved fix is the evidence. Without it, there would be nothing to compare with the human fix.

practice.q: Finish the rule for the stage a run really uses.
practice.after: of the charter's stage and the override flag.
practice.hint: The flag exists to make a routine step down quickly.
practice.why: The override can only lower the stage. Raising it needs a reviewed PR to the charter.

practice.q: A routine has 12 closed PRs and 4 of them merged. Is it demoted for its merge rate?

options.why: With fewer than 20 closed PRs there is no verdict at all. A few PRs are not enough evidence to punish a new routine.

options.text: No, because mergeRate gives no verdict with fewer than 20 closed PRs
options.why: The rule looks at the last 20 closed PRs, and returns undefined until there are 20.

options.text: No, because merge rate only matters for promotion
options.why: It matters for demotion, and for the auto-pause. It is not one of the promotion rules.

practice.q: A routine in normal had one of its PRs reverted yesterday. Put what happens in order.
items: The daily ladder job finds a 'Revert' commit on main that names the routine's PR
demotionReason returns the revert as the reason
The job writes the stage_override flag one step lower, at drafts
The job opens a PR that lowers stage: in the charter, and messages the owner
The next run reads the effective stage, drafts, and opens only a draft PR
practice.why: The flag acts first so the very next run is safer; the charter PR follows so the file stays the truth.

practice.q: Finish the name of the flag that steps a routine down at once, before its charter PR is reviewed.
practice.hint: Two words joined by an underscore: what it changes, and what it does to the charter's value.
practice.why: The stage_override flag can only lower the stage. The next run reads the lower of the charter's stage and this flag.
